correctness.rationale: For the unit-rate nearest-neighbor generator on infinite Z^d, d≥2 and all t>0, P_{d,t}(x)=e^{-2dt}∏_j I_|x_j|(2t) and q=PΣ_j s_|x_j|. The identity r_m′(z)=1−r_m(z)^2−(2m+1)r_m(z)/z and its first-zero derivative argument give r_m′>0; hence s_m strictly increases with |m| and the smallest off-origin score occurs only at the 2d neighbors. The Fourier identity P′_{d,t}(e1)=∫λ(λ/(2d)−1)e^{−λt}dρ splits positive λ>2d from negative λ<2d: the positive/negative Laplace-transform ratio is strictly decreasing from >1 to 0, proving a unique crossing. The origin remains strictly negative; before/at the crossing all other sites are positive/zero at neighbors. The zero-mass kernel then has total variation −2q(0)=4d e^{−2dt}I0(2t)^{d−1}(I0−I1), the exact ℓ1 and ℓ∞ convolution norms; immediately and permanently afterward negative neighbors make it strictly larger. Since s0<0 the crossing decreases in d. The correct small-t ratio R=t−t^3/2+t^5/3+O(t^7), with the root derivative of order −4d², gives τ_d=1/(2d)+1/(4d²)+1/(8d³)+O(d^−4). No unproved infinite inference is made from finite diagnostics.

value.rationale: The first instant at which discrete heat flux reverses sign outside the source is an intrinsically motivated crossover in a canonical infinite graph semigroup. Its location governs the maximal interval of an exact endpoint ℓ1/ℓ∞ operator norm equality, not merely a numerical special-function root. A uniform all-dimensional uniqueness, strict dimension monotonicity and controlled high-dimensional asymptotics would be useful for sharp endpoint semigroup estimates and comparative lattice heat flow. Neither the 1D kernel identity nor elementary normalization by itself gives this exact boundary.
